The paper considers a dual function radar and communication (DFRC) base station equipped with N movable antenna elements.
The transmitter area is quantized into M possible discrete positions, with a minimum distance of D_min between any pair of MA elements.
The paper models the dynamic nature of the radar cross-section (RCS) using the Swerling model, in contrast to existing ISAC literature that assumes a constant and known RCS.
The optimization problem aims to minimize the total transmit power at the base station while ensuring the individual communication and sensing task quality of service requirements.
The proposed solution approach is an iterative alternating optimization algorithm that jointly optimizes the MA positions and the communication/sensing beamformers.
Simulations show that the proposed MA-enhanced ISAC system can significantly reduce the base station transmit power compared to baseline methods, especially as the transmitter area is expanded.

Stricter sensing quality of service requirements (e.g., 1% probability of failure) lead to higher transmit power, but the proposed scheme still outperforms the baseline schemes even for these stricter requirements.

As the normalized transmitter area size increases, the performance benefits of the proposed scheme continue to improve up to a size of 3 for relaxed sensing QoS requirements, while the benefits start to saturate for stricter requirements.
The paper introduces binary position selection variables and a minimum distance constraint to capture the discrete nature of the possible MA positions.

The sensing performance metric is the mean square error between the ideal beam pattern and the actual beam pattern, with chance constraints used to ensure the desired sensing SNR is achieved with a pre-defined probability.

The proposed scheme outperforms the baseline schemes that use fixed antenna positions or antenna selection, as the flexible MA positioning allows for better spatial correlations and interference management.
The paper's joint optimization of MA positions and communication/sensing beamformers is a key contribution, addressing the challenge of the resulting non-convex mixed integer non-linear program.
The consideration of dynamic RCS fluctuations, modeled using the Swerling model, is another important contribution that sets this work apart from existing ISAC literature.
The iterative alternating optimization algorithm developed in the paper is a practical solution approach to tackle the non-convex optimization problem with polynomial time computational complexity.
The simulation results demonstrate the multifaceted benefits of exploiting movable antennas in ISAC systems, including significant power savings and robustness to RCS fluctuations.
